sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Dickson County, TN?
sections.html:
Two county offices split the work. The Assessor of Property, Jenny Heath Martin, discovers, lists, classifies and values every taxable property, and the Trustee, Glynda Pendergrass, bills and collects the tax. The county commission, a body of twelve members, sets the rate each year.

The Assessor's office is in the Dickson County Administration Building at 4 Court Square, P.O. Box 270, Charlotte, TN 37036, phone (615) 789-7015, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The Trustee works from the Charlotte courthouse at 4 Court Square (P.O. Box 220, phone (615) 789-7006) and from a branch at the County Government Building, 303 Henslee Drive in Dickson, phone (615) 446-8293, option 3. Both are open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

The Trustee's FAQ gives P.O. Box 246 in Charlotte for mailed checks or money orders, and a drop box sits at the Henslee Drive location. Use the street addresses for visits and questions.

sections.h2: When are Dickson County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills go out in October, and you can pay from the first Monday of October through the last day of February without interest. The tax covers the calendar year, and the bill is mailed to the owner of record as of January 1.

Property tax calendar for Dickson County owners
DateWhat happens
January 1Assessment date; ownership and values are fixed as of this day
Mid to late MayAssessments complete and change notices mailed (by May 20)
June 1County Board of Equalization convenes
First Monday in OctoberCurrent-year taxes become due and payable
February 28Last day to pay without interest
March 1Taxes become delinquent

Source: Tennessee Comptroller assessment schedule and the Dickson County Trustee FAQ.

Partial payments on the current year are accepted as long as the bill is paid in full by the February deadline, and prepayment by ACH is available. Local banks take current-year payments too, but only in full and only with the tax notice in hand. Your mortgage company does not get a copy of the bill from the county, so forward it yourself if the lender pays your taxes.

sections.h2: What happens if Dickson County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes become delinquent on March 1 and carry interest of one and a half percent a month, which the Trustee puts at 18 percent a year. The Trustee keeps the delinquent account for one year.

After that, the file goes to Dickson County Chancery Court and the delinquent tax attorney, and court costs and fees pile up on top of the interest. When the suit ends, the county can hold a tax sale to sell the property and recover what is owed. A seller who has fallen behind should clear the balance, or have the closing agent pay it from proceeds, before the account reaches that point.

Bankruptcy changes the picture. The Trustee files a claim when it receives a bankruptcy notice, and under federal law it cannot collect real or personal property tax until the case is dismissed or discharged. Taxes are generally paid in installments approved by the court.

sections.h2: Who pays the tax when a Dickson County house is sold?
sections.html:
The Trustee's FAQ states that if a property is bought or sold during the tax year, the purchaser is responsible for any tax not paid at closing. The tax bill goes to whoever owned the property on January 1, and a new owner receives a courtesy copy if a deed change happens after that date.

The FAQ tells new owners to ask the title company or read the closing statement to see who pays the current year's tax. In practice, the sales contract and closing statement divide the bill between seller and buyer, and the title company pays the Trustee. Ask the Trustee at (615) 789-7006 for a duplicate bill, because failing to receive one does not excuse a taxpayer from paying.

When a deed is recorded the Register of Deeds, Shelly Yates, at 4 Court Square in Charlotte (phone (615) 789-5123), adds the transfer to the public record. The register's page says electronic recording is accepted through Simplifile, CSC and ePN. A wrong name or mailing address on the bill is corrected through the Assessor at (615) 789-7015.

sections.h2: How can you appeal a Dickson County assessment or get tax relief?
sections.html:
A disputed value goes first to the Local Board of Equalization. The Trustee's FAQ says the board meets during the first two weeks of June by appointment through the Assessor's office, and the Comptroller's schedule shows the county board convening June 1.

If the county board does not settle it, the State Board of Equalization takes appeals filed by August 1 of the tax year or within 45 days of the date the local board's notice was sent, whichever is later. The State Board first hears the case before an administrative judge.

  • An informal review by the Assessor can be quicker, but the Comptroller says it is not an appeal and does not save your later rights
  • Residential property is assessed at 25 percent of appraised value and commercial or industrial at 40 percent
  • Tax is the assessed value divided by 100, times the rate

For 2026 the state tax relief program covers homeowners who are 65 or older by December 31, disabled homeowners, and disabled veterans or surviving spouses. Elderly and disabled owners must have a 2025 income of $38,470 or less, and relief is calculated on up to $33,600 of market value. Disabled veterans have no income test, and relief is figured on up to $175,000 of value. Apply to the Trustee after you receive the 2026 bill; the deadline is 35 days after the delinquency date, and the tax must be paid by then.

sections.h2: What is Dickson County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Dickson County was created in 1803 and named for William Dickson, a Nashville physician and legislator. Charlotte is the seat and holds what Wikipedia calls Tennessee's oldest courthouse in continuous use, built in 1835. The county covers 491 square miles, with the Cumberland River on the northeast edge and the Harpeth River along the east, and it is part of the Nashville metropolitan area. The county site says six towns are incorporated and calls the drive to Nashville about thirty minutes.

Iron furnaces shaped the early economy, and the railroads built through the south of the county gave rise to Dickson, Tennessee City, White Bluff and Burns. Montgomery Bell State Park, seven miles east of Dickson, is one of the largest state parks in Tennessee. The Dickson County School District serves the whole county with sixteen schools.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts for Dickson County show:

  • 58,662 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up 8.0 percent from the 2020 base
  • 80.3 percent of housing owner-occupied, with median gross rent of $1,015
  • Median home value of $306,400 and median household income of $75,003
  • A mean commute of 32.7 minutes
  • 590 building permits issued in 2025

For a seller with unpaid taxes, a house in need of repairs or an inherited property, the Trustee and the Assessor are the two phone calls to make first, since each can tell you what is owed and how the parcel is valued.

faqs.q: When are Dickson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They can be paid from the first Monday of October and are due without interest through the last day of February. March 1 is the delinquency date, after which interest of 1.5 percent a month applies.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my Dickson County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Dickson County Trustee, by mail to P.O. Box 246, Charlotte, TN 37036, in person at the Charlotte courthouse or at 303 Henslee Drive in Dickson, or online through the Trustee's payment site. Offices are open 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. weekdays.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for the tax if I sell my Dickson County house mid-year?
faqs.a: The buyer is responsible for any tax not paid at closing, according to the Trustee. The sales contract and closing statement decide how the year's bill is split between buyer and seller.

faqs.q: How do I contest my Dickson County property value?
faqs.a: Appear before the Local Board of Equalization, which meets in the first two weeks of June by appointment through the Assessor's office at (615) 789-7015. A further appeal goes to the State Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: Is there property tax relief for seniors in Dickson County?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners who are 65 or older and whose 2025 income is $38,470 or less can apply for state tax relief through the Trustee. Disabled homeowners qualify on the same income limit, and disabled veterans have no income limit.
